found_values.value: 65,535 rpm, the highest speed the BENCH rpm register carries: to_u16 saturates there. The owner's answer to V225 uses the same figure as the highest rpm ('2.54 µs of delay variation at 65,535 rpm'). found_values.value: A Hall-effect bipolar latch with a digital output, selected by R11, on a sensor board of its own that JLCPCB assembles (as V221), supplied at 3.3 V from the IO board's logic rail. An open-drain output is pulled up to 3.3 V on the IO board, or a push-pull output runs from the same 3.3 V, so it never drives an RP2354B pin above the rail and needs no translation. A latch switches on a south pole (BOP) and releases on a north pole (BRP), which V218's two opposite magnets present once a turn.
found_values.source: DRV5015 datasheet SBAS915A, sections 1 and 7 (digital latch, 2.5 to 5.5 V, open-drain), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv5015.pdf (read 2026-09-29T02:49:43Z); checkout e13f5f60d2e5: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:105 (3.3 V logic at every RP2354B pin); hardware/docs/Research.md:134-139 (sourcing rule 1)

found_values.value: One pulse per revolution, from two equal magnets of opposite polarity fixed 180° apart on the rotating part; the latch sees one south and one north pole a turn. Two equal masses at equal radius 180° apart add no static unbalance as far as their masses and radii match, which the balancing guide's rule against mass on the bell asks for. Reading the rotor's own poles (MOTOR_POLES / 2 pulses, up to 21) would put the latch at 22,937 Hz at 65,535 rpm, above the guaranteed bandwidth of every latch found (20 kHz minimum for DRV5015 and DRV5013, 0 to 10 kHz for TLE4961-1M). With one pulse a turn the highest rate is 1,092 Hz and the reading does not use MOTOR_POLES.

found_values.value: The frequency of each of A and B, in Hz. Encoder datasheets state the highest rate per channel: Broadcom's 'Count Frequency f 100 kHz, Velocity (rpm) x N/60' with N in cycles per revolution; US Digital's 'Max. found_values.value: 8 to 288 kHz, wider than the 24, 48 and 96 kHz the programmer screen offers. AM32 takes a PWM frequency setting from 8 to 144 kHz (pwm_frequency < 145 && > 7; TIMER1_MAX_ARR = TIM1_AUTORELOAD × 400 / (setting × 100 / 6), that is TIM1_AUTORELOAD × 24 / setting), and its variable-PWM mode 1 maps the auto-reload between TIMER1_MAX_ARR / 2 and TIMER1_MAX_ARR, up to twice the setting. The list k_pwm (24, 48, 96 kHz) is the PWM frequency choice of all three firmware tables on the programmer screen: BLHeli_S, AM32 and ESCape32. The clip passes up to 22,937 Hz (V212 × 21 pole pairs): that overlaps an 8 kHz PWM, so no fixed low-pass separates the two at every setting; against the 24 kHz lower end of the screen's list the margin is 1.05 ×.

report.value: One RP2354B PIO state machine running pico-examples' quadrature_encoder program; no external decoder. Its worst-case sampling loop is 10 cycles, so it reads up to sysclk / 10: 15 Msteps/s at the RP2350's 150 MHz clk_sys. That covers the single-ended form (1 MHz a channel, 4 Mcounts/s) and RS-422 up to 3.75 MHz a channel, not the 5 MHz of F4 (20 Mcounts/s, V227). No quadrature decoder from an allowlisted maker is in the jlcparts copy: the LS7366R, LS7184, LS7183 and LS7083 rows are LSI/CSI. A PWM slice counts only one edge type or level of its B pin, so it gives no direction; its edge counting takes a 5 MHz input, since the datasheet asks only that the high and low periods exceed one system clock period (6.7 ns). The index pulse is captured by a GPIO edge interrupt or counted on a PWM slice's B pin. Not verified: a program that counts A and B edges in two state machines, or a PWM slice beside the PIO program, would reach 20 Mcounts/s; neither is written
report.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/pico-examples/master/pio/quadrature_encoder/quadrature_encoder.pio (read 2026-09-29T02:54:59Z); RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf served from pip-assets.raspberrypi.com (read 02:55:13Z): clk_sys 150 MHz (page 520), section 12.5.2.5 (page 1083); jlcparts copy 2026-09-14 (read-only search); V227

report.value: The clip passes the motor's electrical frequency up to 22,937 Hz (65,535 rpm × 21 pole pairs) and rejects ESC PWM from 8 kHz to 288 kHz (AM32). The bands overlap below 22.9 kHz, so no fixed low-pass meets both at every setting; against the programmer screen's 24 kHz the margin is 1.05 ×. The front end needs a method that does not rest on frequency separation alone, or the owner narrows V212 or V229 for this input. No comparator changes this

1,092 Hz at 65,535 rpm with V218's one pulse a turn. Reading the rotor's own poles (up to 21 pairs) needs 22,937 Hz, above the latches found: DRV5015 and DRV5013 guarantee 20 kHz (30 kHz typical), TLE4961-1M states 0 to 10 kHz

No analogue accelerometer that passes rule 4 at JLCPCB states a delay, phase or delay-drift figure, so none shows V225's delay variation and the function has no survivor. The output pole of the ADXL316, ADXL326 and AD22035 is RFILT × CX. For the ADXL316 at CX 3 nF (1.66 kHz nominal): phase 33.4° and delay 84.9 µs at 1,092 Hz; a 3.8 % change of RFILT × CX moves the phase by 1°, 2.54 µs, the whole chain's budget. RFILT is 27 to 37 kΩ at 25 °C (8.2° of phase between units at 1,092 Hz, a constant per unit that the trial run cancels); its temperature coefficient and the resonance's Q are not stated. The datasheet recommends CX of 4.7 nF or more, which puts the pole at 1,058 Hz (32 kΩ), under 1,092 Hz; Table 1 note 5 gives 3 nF for 1.6 kHz. The 2 m lead's capacitance (cable not chosen, round 2) adds to CX. The owner decides whether a stated output pole with an unstated drift is accepted for the accelerometer, or whether the chain measures its own delay (for example through the self-test input)
report.source: ADXL316 Rev. C Table 1 and page 11, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/adxl316.pdf (read 2026-09-29T02:41:44Z); ADXL326 Rev. 0 Table 1 (02:41:44Z); ADXL103/ADXL203 Rev. F Table 1 (02:54:45Z); V225; phase = atan(f / fc), 1° at 1,092.25 Hz = 2.543 µs

report.value: The index pulse's front end is in V225's chain. No reflective sensor found states a delay-variation figure: VCNT2030 gives rise 10 µs and fall 15 µs typical at RL 100 Ω, TCND5000 15 ns at IF 100 mA, TCRT5000 and CNY70 no time at all. The optical index therefore has no survivor. The comparator's share is bounded: TLV3201 55 ns and TLV3601 4.5 ns maximum over temperature. The owner decides whether the sensor's share is budgeted by measurement or accepted unstated

report.value: TLV3201 (signal inputs −0.5 V to VCC + 0.5 V) and TLV3601 (VEE − 0.3 V to VCC + 0.3 V) clamp their inputs to both rails, so with the 3.3 V rail down a coasting motor's divided phase signal flows into the rail through the divider's resistance, limited to 10 mA by the datasheets. TLV7011 (inputs VEE − 0.3 V to 6 V, clamped to VEE only) avoids that but states no maximum delay. Round 2 sizes the divider so the current stays under the rating
